data_quality.outlier_policy: No rows removed. thumbs_up outliers are genuine heavily-upvoted reviews (kept, handled with medians / log1p / rank statistics); review_length and sentiment_compound outliers are plausible.

july_check.verdict: No common July shift in the full review stream; a time-based test split is safe.

version_analysis.flag_rule: |z| >= 3 AND |gap| >= 0.25 stars vs the app's mean
version_analysis.caveat: Reviews are attributed to the reviewer's installed version, not necessarily the version that caused the problem.

april_gap.rule: affected = positive reviews/day in the gap < 60% of the before/after average AND fallen to less than 0.6x the relative level of negative reviews/day

definition.note: Payment & Refund can be an app, bank or gateway problem, so it is a separate group. Keyword tags, not human labels.

charts.title: 10 of 11 apps have reviews on all 173 days from 1 Apr 2026; volume ranges 117/day (Google Pay) to 1,539/day (Flipkart); Zomato 172/173 days
charts.subtitle: 1,137,987 reviews in total. Complete weeks only (06 Apr – 20 Sep). Grey band = 21 Apr–05 May feed gap (chart 13). The time window is identical for every app, so apps and weeks compare directly.

charts.title: 67% of reviews are 5★ and 17% are 1★; Amazon is the harshest app (54% 1–2★), PhonePe the mildest (10%)
charts.subtitle: Written reviews sit 0.0–1.4 stars below each app's public rating, which also counts ratings without a written review. App effect on rating: Cramér's V = 0.12.

charts.title: 1★ reviews are 7× longer than 5★ (14 vs 2 words); upvotes are winner-take-all (Gini 0.98)
charts.subtitle: 1★ is 17% of reviews but 59% of upvotes: other users endorse complaints far more than praise. 94% of reviews have no upvotes, so use log(1+upvotes) or medians, never the mean.

charts.title: Rating tracks sentiment (ρ=0.49) and issue tags (ρ=-0.50); issue tags also track review length (ρ=0.46)
charts.subtitle: Spearman rank correlations. Longer text has more chances to match a keyword rule, so the model must not learn length alone.

charts.title: Customer Support is both the most common issue (4.1% of reviews) and the most damaging (1.23★)
charts.subtitle: Bottom-right = frequent AND low-rated. Every issue category is rated below the dataset mean (dashed line).

charts.title: Customer Support leads food & grocery; Cancellation & Return leads shopping; Crash & Stability leads payments; Amazon carries the heaviest issue load
charts.subtitle: % of each app's reviews tagged with the issue (vertical rules separate domains). Strongest app effect: Customer Support (Cramér's V=0.15). All 9 chi-square tests p<0.001.

charts.title: Crash & Stability + UI/UX & Update co-occur 25.7× more than chance (n=281)
charts.subtitle: Pairwise lift = P(A∧B) / (P(A)·P(B)), shown as log2. Blue = issues travel together, red = tend to be mutually exclusive.

charts.title: Tags track rating (49% of 1★ vs 1% of 5★ carry an issue); 5★ 'Cancellation & Return' is the largest false-positive cluster
charts.subtitle: 3,135 five-star reviews carry the Cancellation & Return tag (40% of them Myntra): keyword rules ignore polarity, so praise such as 'easy returns' still matches.

charts.title: 54% of 1–2★ reviews get no issue tag; the most distinctive untagged terms are 'nice product', 'mast', 'ok ok', 'compatible'
charts.subtitle: Untagged low-star reviews are short (median 5 vs 28 words; 30% are 1–2 words), so many carry no issue to tag. Praise words among them point to users who mis-rate. Right-hand labels give the app that uses each term most.

charts.title: From May–Jun to Aug–Sep, Amazon worsened most (+9.6 pp 1–2★) and Google Pay improved most (-5.5 pp); 7 of 11 apps move by less than 2.5 pp
charts.subtitle: Complete weeks; grey band = 21 Apr–05 May feed gap, excluded from the comparison (chart 13). Differences between apps (Cramér's V = 0.12) are far larger than any app's movement over time.

charts.title: 49 of 544 app versions rate clearly worse than their app's average (≥0.25★ below, z ≤ −3)
charts.subtitle: Eight most-reviewed versions per app, ordered by median review date. Red = flagged worse, dark blue = flagged better, grey = not flagged. Versions need ≥30 reviews; 21 Apr–05 May gap days excluded. Full table: data/eda/version_metrics.csv.

charts.title: Food & Grocery reviews are the most negative (22% 1–2★ vs 13% for Payments); Delivery Delay is the most domain-specific issue
charts.subtitle: Top issue: Food & Grocery – Customer Support; Shopping – Cancellation & Return; Payments – Crash & Stability. Delivery Delay: 3.5% in Food & Grocery vs 0.1% in Payments. Bars sorted by the highest domain.

charts.title: 21 Apr–5 May: in 5 of 11 apps positive reviews fall ~84% while negative reviews fall far less — a feed gap, not an incident
charts.subtitle: Affected: Swiggy, Blinkit, Domino's, Flipkart, Amazon. Short positive reviews ('good', 'nice') are what disappear, so median length jumps. Shares such as '% rated 1–2★' are inflated in this window; counts of negative reviews per day are far less affected. The gap is kept in the dataset and flagged; trend, version and July analyses exclude it.

charts.title: Apps in the same domain differ widely: Food: Swiggy 35% vs Zomato 19%; Shopping: Amazon 54% vs Myntra 10%; Payments: Google Pay 23% vs PhonePe 10%
charts.subtitle: Apps ranked within each domain by % of reviews rated 1–2★; beside each bar are the app's two most frequent issue tags (% of its reviews). Excluding the 21 Apr – 5 May feed gap moves no app by more than 1.6 points, and only Blinkit and Zomato swap order (a near-tie).

charts.title: Among 1–2★ reviews that name an issue, 91% name a service problem and 7% an app problem
charts.subtitle: What each app's 1–2★ reviews are about, from the keyword tags. Service = delivery, order quality, cancellation/return, support, pricing; app = crash, login/OTP, UI/update. Payment & Refund can be the app, a bank or a gateway, so it is shown separately. 54% of 1–2★ reviews carry no tag, so every share here is a lower bound.
